Subject: POC environment: what do you need to close by Sept?

Hey Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was encouraged by the latency numbers. We want to accelerate to a 4-week POC and need a short mutual action plan so we can hit a business decision by early September. From our side we expect to validate: token cost at load, inference latency under 200ms p50 for 256-token prompts, and org-level audit logs.

To plan our network side we need to confirm the Redwood checklist for the POC environment: service API keys (temporary eval keys), Redwood org invite for our engineers, IP allowlist entries (CIDR), and VPC peering details (AWS account/VPC id). Can you provide a simple timeline and the exact artifacts your infra team needs from us?

We'd like to lock a go/no-go decision window the first week of September. Who should I loop on our side for networking? (I'll include them in follow-ups.)

Thanks —
Alice Wong

HealthStart Inc.

Hi Alice — great to hear the demo landed well. Appreciate the clear acceptance criteria. Below is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) distilled to the items your network/security and product teams will need. I've attached a draft MAP and a tiny network template you can fill out.

High level MAP (target: 4 weeks)
- Week 0 (today): Sign MAP draft, confirm point-of-contacts for networking and security.
- Week 1: Org invite + temporary API keys issued (read/test scope).
- Week 1-2: Network window — IP allowlist + VPC peering request initiated by HealthStart.
- Week 2-3: Smoke tests (latency/cost) with your sample prompts; we run side-by-side traces.
- Week 3-4: Quality regression checks & decision window.

What we need from HealthStart network team (minimum)
- AWS account ID and VPC ID(s) for peering
- CIDR(s) to allow in our firewall for API traffic (we generally recommend /28 or smaller per endpoint)
- Contact name/email for peering acceptance/testing

What Redwood will deliver
- Temporary API keys scoped for evaluation, issued within 24 hours of org invite acceptance.
- A Redwood org with role-based invites for up to 6 engineers.
- Peering request from our side and assistance with route table instructions; expected turnaround 48–72 hours once both sides accept.
- A short compliance packet (SOC2 snapshot + logs retention notes) — I'll loop Neha for that.

Attachments: HS_MAP_draft.xlsx (editable MAP), network_template.csv (fields for AWS account, VPC IDs, CIDR ranges).

Next steps: if you can confirm your network contact and fill the template we can get keys and invites started tomorrow. Marcus is on copy and will lead the peering/network coordination.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: POC environment: what do you need to close by Sept?

Alice / Kimberly — quick technical notes on the peering and IP allowlist so your infra team can slot them into a ticket. Posting here so it's in-thread for the MAP doc.

Peering basics (Redwood-hosted inference in AWS us-west-2):
- Redwood will open a VPC peering request to your VPC. To initiate we ask for: AWS account ID, VPC ID, and one routable CIDR for our peering (we also share ours in the peering request).
- No BGP; standard AWS VPC peering. Add a route in your route table for our VPC CIDR -> peering connection. We'll do the symmetric change on our side.
- Security groups: our inference endpoints are behind an internal ALB. For initial eval allowlist, please permit outbound HTTPS to 52.38.90.0/24 (our managed egress range) and 10.20.0.0/16 (our peered VPC private range). If you prefer a single /28, we can provide ephemeral NAT IPs — tell us preference.
- DNS: we can provide private-hosted-zones over the peering if you want FQDNs to resolve privately; this is optional.

Peering operational timeline: after we have the account/VPC IDs and a contact to accept the peering, expected time to establish and verify routes is 1–3 business days. Heavy network change windows or approvals on your side may extend this.

Example peering payload you'll see:
--
RequesterAccount: 123456789012
RequesterVPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e
RequesterCIDR: 10.20.0.0/16
--

If your team uses a change board, let us know the scheduled window and we can align. Also copy in your security ops email if you want the compliance packet up front.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
